source.title: ATLAS: Constitution-Conditioned Latent Geometry and Redistribution Across Language Models and Neural Perturbation Data
source.authors: Gareth Seneque; Lap-Hang Ho; Nafise Erfanian Saeedi; Jeffrey Molendijk; T. Elson

record.file_problem: Whole paper is present and readable. Some tables are flattened, and one MCQ answer-route mean-gap value conflicts between the prose and table/figure; this is noted in the relevant row.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether a frozen source-defined family can be recovered across a language-model change and a biological substrate, and explicitly limits the result to partial family-level recurrence rather than exact identity. Its findings also compare structural and occupancy measures and report a task-dependent failure. It does not test convergence as model scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: Claim-bearing results are the Phi and ALM8 cross-system structural and behavioural evaluations, plus the MCQ boundary and its geometry diagnostics. The Gemma source-side chart and compact-patch results do not compare representations across systems. The paper's additional follow-up findings and cited prior work are not treated as independent rows here.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of representation convergence. It re-identifies one constitution-induced perturbation family across systems: a Gemma adapter-on minus adapter-off hidden-state contrast. The targets are an unadapted Phi model and mouse ALM8 data, with prompt or condition contrasts. The claim-bearing numbers are AUCs and mean gaps separating informative-constitution from null-random-control conditions. The occupancy distances compare those two conditions on the same target site, not one system's representations with another's. The source structure is induced on purpose by constitution fine-tuning. There is no measure of whole-representation alignment between independently trained models, and no scale, cross-modal, seed, mapping-loss or feature-universality test. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis is cited only as motivation. The findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a Gemma-defined, constitution-conditioned family recurs on Phi and in held-out ALM8 data as 'family-level structural correspondence with redistribution'. They deny exact identity, coordinate identity and target-side mediation. They treat MCQ as the limiting case, where localisation occurs without source-faithful closure.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a bespoke frozen-family, local-chart and tangent/occupancy validation protocol rather than the cited representation-convergence methods. It does not perform a model-scale sweep or an explicit reproduction of the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on the structural metric: chart/tangent support can pass while occupancy support fails. It also varies by evaluation route: the primary Phi policy comparison is strong, the secondary route weaker, and the MCQ paired routes wrong-signed.

fits_no_version.finding: A Gemma constitution-conditioned perturbation subspace family is re-identified in unadapted Phi-4 Mini under prompt conditions. Chart support passes and occupancy is blocked. The behavioural separation has AUC 0.984 on the policy route, AUC 0.622 on the secondary route, and is wrong-signed on MCQ (AUC 0.43/0.45).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-induced local representational structure in one LLM can be partly re-identified, as a structurally similar subspace, in another LLM.

fits_no_version.finding: The same frozen family yields positive held-out separation in ALM8 mouse frontal-cortex data: mean AUC 0.72, gap 4.50, 5/5 folds positive. Chart support holds on 5/5 folds and occupancy on 4/5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-derived local subspace families correspond partially to structure in biological neural perturbation data.

record.problems: No scale or capability comparison is made, so the study cannot address convergence increasing with size or performance. The main cross-model claim is a frozen-family re-identification rather than direct alignment of whole-model representations. Phi confirmatory review uses a single adjudicator. The paper reports incomplete occupancy closure and a weaker secondary Phi route; the MCQ answer-route mean-gap prose conflicts with its table and figure.
record.rows_left_out: Gemma source-local anchor, source-family support, and exact-patch results were left out because they are source-side analyses rather than cross-system alignment results. Supporting analyses on Llama 3.1, Qwen3, Mouse95, ALM7, and Pyramid were also left out; the paper identifies them as supporting or interpretive rather than co-equal confirmatory routes. See Sections 3 and 7 and Appendix D.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no whole-representation alignment between independently trained models.
No map, stitching or relative-representation loss is measured.
No recurrence of interpretable units, SAE features or circuits.
No convergence measure is compared across metrics, neighbour settings or input distributions. Chart and occupancy are the study's own thresholds for a perturbation subspace.
No degree or plateau of cross-model alignment is measured, and no test of shared data or objectives as the cause.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V6 and V7, but the study's measures are behavioural condition separations and within-target occupancy between conditions. None is a representational alignment between independently trained systems. Supporting Llama, Qwen, Mouse95, ALM7 and Pyramid analyses are interpretive only. Single adjudicator for the Phi labels.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep and no test of whether alignment rises with scale or performance.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different random initializations.
The study re-identifies a source-defined family as a target-local structure, but does not test a representation map, stitching, relative representations, or paired-data-free mapping with little loss.
No recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits is tested.

The study compares chart/tangent and occupancy measures and reports differing outcomes across Phi and MCQ routes. It does not sweep settings such as neighbour count, nor comprehensively test out-of-distribution inputs.
The study reports incomplete correspondence and a failing MCQ route, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, or whether alignment plateaus with scale.

relation.reason: Section 1.4 uses representation convergence, similarity and transfer as motivation. The experiments test the study's separate frozen-family correspondence contract.

tranche.reason: The study measures recurrence of a deliberately induced constitution-conditioned family and separation of condition contrasts. It does not test scale-dependent alignment, independent-seed convergence, interchangeable representations, recurring interpretable features, or the catalog's metric/data and causal explanations of convergence.

source_check.notes: The authors' bounded family-level correspondence conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Canonical Phi lane terminology varies between reason and late_reason; Table 18 explicitly identifies layer 24 reason, supporting the listed face.
